test_title: PYST 24: SSC CGL 2024 - Quantitative Aptitude (Held On: 19 Sept, 2024 Shift 3)
subject: maths
question: Find the gain percentage, given that Anubha sold her scooter for ₹23358 gaining (1)/(6)th of the selling price.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When profit is given as a fraction of Selling Price (SP), the actual SP value (₹23358) is not needed.

Given Gain = 1/6 of SP.

Let SP = 6 units, then Gain = 1 unit.

Cost Price (CP) = SP − Gain = 6 − 1 = 5 units.

Gain % = (Gain ÷ CP) × 100 = (1 ÷ 5) × 100 = 20%.

**∴ The correct answer is 20%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Selling Price (SP) = ₹23358

Gain = 1/6 of SP

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7c1fbbcf749239d3b0244e359996f6de68c4a17fcce784f0cbd89d78a63c40ae.png] 

**Formula Used:**

Gain = SP − CP

Gain % = (Gain ÷ CP) × 100

**Calculations:**

⇒ Gain = (1 ÷ 6) × 23358 = ₹3893

⇒ CP = SP − Gain

⇒ CP = 23358 − 3893 = ₹19465

⇒ Gain % = (3893 ÷ 19465) × 100

⇒ Gain % = (1 ÷ 5) × 100 = 20%

**∴ The correct answer is 20%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Profit/Loss on Selling Price

Sometimes profit or loss is stated as a percentage of the Selling Price, but actual profit/loss percentage must always be calculated on the Cost Price (CP). True Profit % = Profit ÷ (SP − Profit) × 100.

Marked Price & Discount

Discount is always calculated on the Marked Price (MP). Equivalent discount of two successive discounts d₁% and d₂% is given by (d₁ + d₂ − d₁×d₂÷100)%.

Dishonest Dealer

If a trader sells goods at cost price but uses a false weight, the Profit % = (True Weight − False Weight) ÷ False Weight × 100.
